title: Fair Class-Incremental Learning using Sample Weighting

problem.claim: Naively training on all current-task samples can cause unfair catastrophic forgetting for certain sensitive groups, including classes.

gap.claim: Fairness has received relatively less study than accuracy in class-incremental learning.

contributions.claim: The paper analyzes forgetting in terms of the inner product between the average gradient vectors of current-task data and sensitive groups.
The paper proposes a fair class-incremental learning framework that adjusts current-task sample weights to change the average gradient direction and reduce forgetting for underperforming groups.
The paper formulates fairness optimization problems and proposes an efficient Fairness-aware Sample Weighting algorithm solvable with linear programming.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that FSW achieves better accuracy-fairness tradeoffs than state-of-the-art approaches on real datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fairness is identified as important in class-incremental learning for Trustworthy AI.
The abstract characterizes fairness as understudied relative to accuracy.
Using all current-task samples naively can produce unfair catastrophic forgetting for certain sensitive groups.
The paper links forgetting to opposing average gradient directions, then uses sample weighting, fairness optimization, linear programming, and FSW to address it.
Experiments are reported to show improved accuracy-fairness tradeoffs on real datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links forgetting of sensitive groups to negative inner products between current-task and group-average gradient vectors.

interpretation.claim: Gradient-direction alignment may provide a mechanism for diagnosing or reducing group-specific forgetting.

application.claim: When adapting this idea, monitor group-specific gradient relationships and consider weighting samples to alter harmful aggregate directions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this mechanism applies beyond the described class-incremental learning setting.

source_observation.claim: The framework formulates fairness objectives that minimize overall sensitive-group losses while minimizing disparities among groups.

interpretation.claim: Fairness objectives can be incorporated directly into sample-weight optimization rather than evaluated only after training.

application.claim: For related incremental-learning systems, define group-loss and disparity objectives before optimizing training weights.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the fairness measures, optimization constraints, or conditions under which the approach is effective.

unknowns: The specific datasets, baselines, fairness measures, and numerical results are not given.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, or limitations.
